title: Nimisha Sajayan's Babita Singh Reporting Premieres on Prime Video August 28
excerpt: The investigative drama from Paatal Lok creator Sudip Sharma marks Nimisha Sajayan's Hindi debut alongside Barun Sobti.
body:
• Babita Singh Reporting premieres globally on Prime Video on August 28 in Hindi with English subtitles
  • Nimisha Sajayan makes her Hindi debut as a suspended cop investigating a childhood friend's murder
  • The film is executive produced by Sudip Sharma, the creator of Paatal Lok, and directed by Ambiecka Pandit
  • Barun Sobti and Anshumaan Pushkar round out the lead cast in the Prime Original movie

Prime Video has set August 28 as the global premiere date for Babita Singh Reporting, an investigative drama that marks Malayalam star Nimisha Sajayan's first Hindi-language project. The film will stream across India and more than 240 countries and territories.

A Suspended Cop, a Dead Friend, and a Small-Town Murder

Sajayan plays Babita — known as Baby — a suspended police officer in a small Indian town. When a childhood friend is murdered, Baby is drawn into an investigation that quickly becomes personal. As she digs deeper into the killing, the case forces her to confront her own choices, relationships, and the life she has built around the expectations of others.

Prime Video describes the film as a blend of murder investigation and grounded realism, layered with complex family dynamics. At its core, the story is about a woman attempting to reclaim her voice while navigating grief and duty.

The Team Behind Paatal Lok Returns

The creative pedigree behind Babita Singh Reporting is substantial. Sudip Sharma, the writer behind NH10, Udta Punjab, and both seasons of Prime Video's acclaimed Paatal Lok, serves as executive producer. Ambiecka Pandit directs from a screenplay by Amita Vyas.

"The movie unfolds around a crime, but at its heart, it is also about the personal journey of a woman who has always adjusted, sought validation from others, and stayed in the background of her own life."

— Sudip Sharma, Executive Producer

The film is produced by Saurabh Malhotra, Manuj Mittra, and Tina Tharwani under Film Squad Productions, in association with Act Three.

A Cast Built for the Story

Sajayan, celebrated for powerful performances in Malayalam films like The Great Indian Kitchen and her recent Hindi OTT appearance in Dabba Cartel, takes the central role. Barun Sobti, known for Iss Pyaar Ko Kya Naam Doon and Tanhaiyan, plays a pivotal role alongside her, while Anshumaan Pushkar adds depth to the ensemble.

Nikhil Madhok, director and head of originals at Prime Video India, called the film "a strong testament to our vision of championing stories that are distinctive, authentic, and emotionally engaging."

Why It Matters for Indian Streaming

Babita Singh Reporting arrives at a time when Prime Video is aggressively expanding its Indian original slate. The platform recently announced The Revolutionaries premiering September 11 and renewed Adarsh Baal Vidyalaya for two more seasons. The film also represents a growing trend of Malayalam talent crossing over into Hindi-language OTT projects, with Sajayan joining a wave of South Indian actors and filmmakers finding new audiences on streaming platforms.

For diaspora audiences, the film's global day-and-date release across 240-plus countries means no wait for availability outside India — a shift that has become standard for Prime Video's Indian originals.
